origin.description: An ordinary or balanced bootstrap, then importance resampling from exponentially tilted or frequency-smoothed weights.
origin.usage:
tilt.boot(data, statistic, R, sim = "ordinary", stype = "i",
          strata = rep(1, n), L = NULL, theta = NULL,
          alpha = c(0.025, 0.975), tilt = TRUE, width = 0.5,
          index = 1, ...)

arguments.name: data
arguments.text: A vector, matrix, or data frame. Each row of a matrix or data frame is one observation.

arguments.name: statistic
arguments.text: Function of the data and a second argument of indices, weights, or frequencies. Further arguments are passed through unchanged.

arguments.name: R
arguments.text: Replicate counts. The first is the uniform bootstrap; 0 skips it. Each later count is the number of draws from one tilted distribution. The length is one more than the length of theta.

arguments.name: sim
arguments.text: "ordinary" or "balanced". Any other value is an error.

arguments.name: stype
arguments.text: "i" for indices, "w" for weights, or "f" for frequencies.

arguments.name: strata
arguments.text: Stratum labels, one per observation. The default is a single sample, and it is evaluated after the sample size is known.

arguments.name: L
arguments.text: Empirical influence values, used only when tilt is TRUE. If omitted they are estimated.

arguments.name: theta
arguments.text: Means for the tilted distributions. Required when the first replicate count is 0. Otherwise the alpha quantiles of the uniform bootstrap are used.

arguments.name: alpha
arguments.text: Quantile levels used to choose theta from the uniform bootstrap. Ignored when theta is supplied. A warning is given when the first count is 0, and another when a level is so extreme that fewer than about five uniform replicates fall beyond it.

arguments.name: tilt
arguments.text: TRUE uses exponential tilting. FALSE uses frequency smoothing, which requires a positive first replicate count.

arguments.name: width
arguments.text: Bandwidth passed to smooth.f when tilt is FALSE.

arguments.name: index
arguments.text: 1-based component of the statistic used to tilt. Only the first element is used.
Further arguments passed to statistic on every call.

origin.details: The first stage, when requested, is an ordinary or balanced bootstrap with equal weights. Tilting then recentres the linear approximation at theta, or frequency smoothing builds a nearby distribution on the sample. A second bootstrap draws from those weights. The returned replicates stack the uniform stage in front of the tilted stages. Random numbers are the package generator, the same sequence as set.seed.
origin.value: A bootstrap object. Extra components are the weight matrix, one row per distribution, and theta. The first weight row is uniform when the first replicate count is positive.
origin.example:
set.seed(2)
x <- c(1.2, 3.4, 2.2, 5.0, 4.1, 0.7)
tb <- tilt.boot(x, function(d, i) mean(d[i]), R = c(20, 15), theta = 3.5)
print(tb$t0)
print(tb$R)
print(tb$theta)
print(c(tb$t))

translation.description: An ordinary or balanced bootstrap, then importance resampling from exponentially tilted or frequency-smoothed weights.
translation.usage: tilt_boot(data, statistic, R, sim="ordinary", stype="i", strata=None, L=None, theta=None, alpha=None, tilt=True, width=0.5, index=1, **kwargs)

arguments.name: data
arguments.text: A vector, a two-dimensional array with one row per observation, or a dict of columns.

arguments.name: statistic
arguments.text: Function of the data and a second argument of 1-based indices, weights, or frequencies. Further keyword arguments are passed through unchanged.

arguments.name: R
arguments.text: Replicate counts. The first is the uniform bootstrap; 0 skips it. Each later count is the number of draws from one tilted distribution. The length is one more than the length of theta.

arguments.name: sim
arguments.text: "ordinary" or "balanced". Any other value is an error.

arguments.name: stype
arguments.text: "i" for 1-based indices, "w" for weights, or "f" for frequencies.

arguments.name: strata
arguments.text: Stratum labels, one per observation. None is a single sample, filled in after the sample size is known.

arguments.name: L
arguments.text: Empirical influence values, used only when tilt is True. If omitted they are estimated.

arguments.name: theta
arguments.text: Means for the tilted distributions. Required when the first replicate count is 0. Otherwise the alpha quantiles of the uniform bootstrap are used.

arguments.name: alpha
arguments.text: Quantile levels used to choose theta from the uniform bootstrap. The default is 0.025 and 0.975. Ignored when theta is supplied. A warning is given when the first count is 0, and another when a level is so extreme that fewer than about five uniform replicates fall beyond it.

arguments.name: tilt
arguments.text: True uses exponential tilting. False uses frequency smoothing, which requires a positive first replicate count.

arguments.name: width
arguments.text: Bandwidth passed to smooth_f when tilt is False.

arguments.name: index
arguments.text: 1-based component of the statistic used to tilt. Only the first element is used.

arguments.name: **kwargs
arguments.text: Further arguments passed to statistic on every call.

translation.details: The uniform stage and the tilted stage are boot.resample.boot. Tilting recentres the linear approximation at theta; frequency smoothing builds a nearby distribution on the sample. Replicates stack the uniform stage in front of the tilted stages. Draws use boot.rng, the same sequence as set_seed and R set.seed.
translation.value: The bootstrap object from the uniform stage, or a stand-in when that stage is skipped. t stacks every stage, weights has one row per distribution, R is the input counts, and theta is the tilted means.
translation.example:
import numpy as np
from boot.rng import set_seed
from boot.tilt import tilt_boot

def statistic(data, indices):
    values = np.asarray(data, float)[np.asarray(indices, int) - 1]
    return float(values.mean())

set_seed(2)
result = tilt_boot(
    [1.2, 3.4, 2.2, 5.0, 4.1, 0.7],
    statistic,
    R=[20, 15],
    theta=3.5,
)
print(float(np.asarray(result.t0).reshape(-1)[0]))
print(np.asarray(result.R))
print(np.asarray(result.theta))
print(np.asarray(result.t).reshape(-1))
